# Tobit Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_002_page_001.jpg

---

**2:1** And in-the days of Sarchedonus I-returned to my-house and my-wife Anna was-restored to-me and Tobias my-son. And at-the feast of Weeks — which is the holy Pentecost — there-was for-me a good dinner and I-reclined-at-table.

**2:2** And a table was-set for-me and there-were-set-before-me many things to-eat; and I-said to Tobias my-son: "Child, go and bring whomever you shall-find among our brothers the poor ones who remembers the LORD, and I will eat together-with him. Behold, I wait for-you, my child, until-you-come-back."

**2:3** And Tobias went to-seek a poor-man from our brothers, and he-returned and said: "Father, one of our race has-been-strangled and has-been-thrown-out in-the market-place, and he-is lying there."

**2:4** And before I-tasted anything I-leaped-up and I-took-up him to a room until the-sun went-down.

**2:5** And having-returned, I-washed myself and ate my-bread in-grief.

**2:6** And I-remembered the word of Amos the-prophet, as he-said: "Your feasts shall-be-turned into grief and all-your songs into lamentation." And I-wept.

**2:7** And when the-sun went-down, I-went and dug a grave and buried him.

**2:8** And my-neighbors were-mocking at-me and were-saying: "Still he-is not afraid. Already before he-has-fled on-account-of this, and see, he-is-burying the-dead again."

**2:9** And that-same night I-washed myself and entered into my-courtyard and I-slept beside-the wall of my-courtyard, and my-face was-uncovered on-account-of the-heat.

**2:10** And I-did-not-know that sparrows were in-the wall above-me, and their warm-droppings fell into my-eyes and produced white-films; and I-was-going to-the physicians and they-were not-helping me. And Achiacharus was-feeding me until he-went into Elymais.

**2:11** And my-wife Anna was-working at-women's-tasks and was-sending [goods] to those-who-hired and was-receiving wages in-return. On the seventh of Dystros, when she-cut-off and sent to-those-who-hired,

**2:12** they paid her her-full-wages and also gave to-her a kid of the-goats for [her] household.

**2:13** And when she-came to-me, the-kid began to-bleat. And calling her, I-said: "From-where [is] this kid? Is-it not stolen? Give [it] back to its-owners, for it-is not permitted to-us to-eat anything stolen."

**2:14** But she-said to-me: "It was-given to-me as a gift in-addition-to my wages." And I-was not-believing her and was-telling her to-give-it-back to its-owners, and I-was-reddening because-of her. Then she-replied and said to-me: "And-where are your acts-of-mercy? And-where are your righteous-deeds? See, all-things are-known about-you!"

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

- 2:1: "feast of Weeks" (pentēkostē) — the Greek uses both the Hebrew-calendar name and its Greek equivalence (Pentecost); EMET preserves both as the text does.
- 2:2: "who remembers the LORD" — the Greek has memnēmenon, "one who is mindful." The object "the LORD" is implied; EMET brackets it, but in fact the Greek has no explicit divine object, only tou kyriou in some manuscripts. Sinaiticus reads simply "mindful."
- 2:3: "strangled" (pepnigmenos) — not murdered; could refer to execution by strangulation or simply a corpse found with marks of violence. Some translate "murdered" but the Greek is specific.
- 2:4: "to a room" — the Greek reads "to one of the rooms" (eis tina oikēma); EMET simplifies slightly.
- 2:6: The Amos citation (Amos 8:10) is slightly adapted: "Your feasts shall be turned into mourning and all your songs into lamentation." The Greek here differs slightly from the LXX Amos text, suggesting Tobit's author quoted from memory or a variant.
- 2:10: "white films" (leukōmata) — cataracts or corneal scarring; the specific eye condition. "Warm droppings" (thermē) — literally "warm things/droppings."
- 2:11: "Dystros" — the Macedonian month corresponding to approximately February-March.
- 2:14: "I-was-reddening" — Greek ērythriazon, "I blushed/was ashamed/turned red"; used for both shame and anger. The ambiguity may be intentional.

*— EMET*
